definitions.explanation: animal feces, used especially for animal droppings rather than human waste

examples.japanese: {犬|いぬ}の{糞|ふん}を{片付|かたづ}けてください。
examples.english: Please clean up the dog droppings.

examples.japanese: {馬|うま}の{糞|ふん}は{肥料|ひりょう}として{使|つか}われる。
examples.english: Horse dung is used as fertilizer.

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}の{遊歩道|ゆうほどう}に{鳥|とり}の{糞|ふん}がたくさん{落|お}ちていて、{歩|ある}きにくかった。
examples.english: There were so many bird droppings on the park walkway that it was hard to walk.

notes:
Primarily used for animal excrement. The reading ふん is the standard neutral/scientific form. The same kanji can also be read くそ, which is vulgar and commonly used as a curse word. Signs in parks saying "{犬|いぬ}の{糞|ふん}は{持|も}ち{帰|かえ}りましょう" (please take your dog's droppings home) are ubiquitous in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {犬|いぬ}の{糞|ふん}: dog droppings
- {鳥|とり}の{糞|ふん}: bird droppings
- {糞|ふん}{尿|にょう}: excrement and urine
- {糞|ふん}{害|がい}: damage from droppings (e.g., pigeon droppings on buildings)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- くそ: shit/crap — same kanji ({糞|くそ}), but vulgar; also used as a curse or intensifier
- {便|べん}: stool — medical/clinical term for human feces
- {排泄物|はいせつぶつ}: excretion — formal term covering all bodily waste
- うんち: poop — childish, informal word used mainly by or with children
